A cause has yet to be definitively determined, but some of the thefts were linked to the use of trading bots like Solareum. According to security researcher Plum, the Solareum Telegram trading bot vulnerability resulted in a loss of assets worth approximately $1 million.

Solareum, a Solana Telegram trading bot, shut down in March 2024 after more than 300 user wallets were drained. Early reports estimated losses near 2,800 SOL, while later court-linked reporting alleged a developer tied to North Korean remote IT worker operations stole about 6,045 SOL from custodied user wallets. The exact technical intrusion path was never publicly disclosed by Solareum. Public reporting and later court-linked allegations indicate that Solareum custodied user private keys and that a developer with privileged internal access allegedly used that access to drain user wallets. Solareum's Telegram trading bot for Solana was exploited on 29 March 2024 through insider access and private key compromise, resulting in reported losses ranging from $523,000 to $1.4 million. The incident involved draining user wallets whose keys had been imported into the bot. Tether and US authorities later froze and seized most of the proceeds, but technical disclosure and chain-level evidence remain limited. Private key custody for user accounts enabled an insider with privileged access to extract and misuse keys, compromising imported SOL wallets. The Solana ecosystem is grappling with a spate of drained wallets. A cause has yet to be definitively determined, but some of the thefts were linked to the use of trading bots like Solareum. Solareum speculated that the exploits may have been linked to compromised Telegram bot tokens, which could have allowed the attackers to obtain private keys from message history. Solareum later wrote that they would be closing the project, and deleted their website. This drew some criticism from users who accused them of doing nothing to investigate the hack, or even being responsible themselves.
